claims.text: In situ tensile testing combined with digital image correlation can effectively characterize the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Digital image correlation can reveal the deformation behavior and failure mechanisms of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The FeNiCrMn alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The FeNiCrMn alloy has excellent corrosion resistance.
A uniaxial tensile load will be applied while the specimen surface is continuously imaged using DIC.
Testing will be performed at room temperature, at a controlled loading rate, and in a standard ambient atmosphere.
A homogeneous grain structure and the alloy's inherent dislocation distribution mediate uniform deformation.
Under tensile loading, the FeNiCrMn alloy deforms through dislocation motion.
Grain-boundary interactions contribute to deformation of the FeNiCrMn alloy under tensile loading.
DIC can quantify local strain variations that correlate with microstructural features.
The experiment will produce a detailed stress-strain curve.
The experiment will produce strain maps that identify regions of strain localization.
The experiment will provide quantitative mechanical properties, including yield strength and ductility.
Existing information on this alloy consists of corrosion-resistance data without a comprehensive mechanical-property evaluation.
The anticipated results are limited to ambient testing conditions.
Behavior at elevated temperatures or under different environmental conditions is uncertain.
Prior investigations of the mechanical behavior of this specific FeNiCrMn alloy are limited.
DIC may not capture all deformation phenomena relevant to the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Nanoindentation could provide complementary information about local mechanical responses.
Post-mortem SEM analysis can correlate deformation features with local strain concentrations measured by DIC.
